args.summary: checkout-api failed health checks after the latest deploy of v2.3.1 to all production regions (18% error rate). Rolled back all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The first rollback attempt was a partial failure (us-east only) due to an orchestrator error; a retry completed the rollout to all regions. Service is now healthy and on v2.3.0 with an error rate of ~0.2%. Root cause of v2.3.1 failure still needs investigation.
args.title: checkout-api health check failures after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0

trace.final:
Done. Summary of what happened and what I did:

**Diagnosis:** checkout-api was unhealthy on v2.3.1 across all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate. Per the release history, v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production.

**Rollback:** Rolled back all regions to v2.3.0. The first attempt was a partial failure — us-east rolled back but the orchestrator halted — so I retried and the rollout completed to all three regions.

**Verification:** checkout-api is now healthy on v2.3.0, error rate down to ~0.2%.

**Incident:** Opened SEV2 incident **INC-0001** ("checkout-api health check failures after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0"), which paged the on-call engineer. The incident notes the failed v2.3.1 release, the rollback and the transient orchestrator error requiring a retry, and flags that the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure still needs investigation.

No change-manager approval was needed since v2.3.0 had been previously healthy in production.
